items.subject: Inclusion of the Pumped Storage Plants (PSPs) in the eligibility list for participation in the High Price Day Ahead Market (HPDAM).
items.pdf_digest:
CENTRAL ELECTRICITY REGULATORY COMMISSION
NEW DELHI
Petition No. 13/SM/2026 (Suo-Motu)
Coram:
Shri Jishnu Barua, Chairperson
Shri Ramesh Babu V, Member
Shri Harish Dudani, Member
Shri Ravinder Singh Dhillon, Member
Date of Order: 28th October, 2026
IN THE MATTER OF:
Inclusion of the Pumped Storage Plants (PSPs) in the eligibility list for participation in
the High Price Day Ahead Market (HPDAM).
ORDER
The High Price Day Ahead Market (HP-DAM) segment was introduced within
the Integrated Day Ahead Market (I-DAM) framework to provide a market avenue for
generating stations with high generation costs, for which the prevailing price ceiling in
the DAM could constrain participation in the power market. In this context, vide
Orders dated 16.02.2023 (Petition No. 359/MP/2022), 11.04.2023 (Petition No.
14/MP/2023) and 24.07.2023 (Petition No. 122/MP/2023), the Commission permitted
the Power Exchanges to introduce HP-DAM with the following categories of
generating stations to participate in the HP-DAM Segment:
(i) Gas-based generating stations using imported RLNG and Naphtha
(ii) Imported coal-based generating stations using only imported coal
(iii) Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS).
2. The Commission further directed the National Load Despatch Centre (NLDC)
vide Order in Petition No. 359/MP/2022 and in Petition No.14/MP/2023, to compile a
list of all the eligible HP-DAM sellers along with recommendations for inclusion of any
Order in Petition No. 13/SM/2026 Page 1 of 7

other resource in the HP-DAM eligibility list. The relevant extract of the Order is as
under:
“We also direct NLDC to compile a list of all such eligible sellers and publish in
their website under intimation to the Commission. NLDC is also directed to submit a
quarterly report with recommendations, if any, for inclusion of any resource or
generating station with any specific fuel source, in the eligibility list for participation in
HP-DAM.”
3. Further, the Ministry of Power (MoP), vide letter dated 10.04.2023, notified the
Guidelines to promote development of Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs), which, inter
alia, provide for participation of PSPs in the HP-DAM segment as under:
“3.4…..(iii) PSPs and other storage projects shall be allowed to participate in
all market segments of the power exchange, including the high price segment of the
Day Ahead Market (HP-DAM) so that they can take suitable advantage of the price
differential between Peak and Off-Peak tariffs.”
4. NLDC, vide letters dated 02.07.2026 and 24.07.2026, recommended to the
Commission for inclusion of Pumped Storage Plants (PSPs) in the eligibility list for
participation in HP-DAM. Subsequently, considering the critical role of PSPs in
providing long-duration energy storage, peak power support, and grid balancing
services, MoP, vide letter dated 30.07.2026, suggested that the Commission
“consider including PSPs as eligible generating stations for participation in the HP-
DAM under the applicable regulatory framework”.
5. In support of the recommendation, NLDC submitted an analysis of the present
PSP capacity, HP-DAM liquidity, levelized tariff of PSPs and the opportunity available
in the DAM. The salient findings of the aforesaid analysis, relevant for consideration
for inclusion of PSPs in HP-DAM, are as under:
(i) As per the report published by CEA in January 2026 on "Roadmap to 100 GW
of Hydro Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs) by 2035-36", the operational PSP
capacity in India stands at 7,425.6 MW. Of the total operational capacity,
4845.6 MW comprises on-stream capacity and 2580 MW comprises off-stream
capacity. NLDC submitted that presently, the operational PSPs are almost fully
Order in Petition No. 13/SM/2026 Page 2 of 7

6. Based on the recommendation and analysis submitted by NLDC, the
Commission is of the prima facie view that, under the prevailing market conditions,
the opportunity available in the present scenario (through the DAM alone) may not be
sufficient for PSPs. We are of the opinion that PSP participation in the HP-DAM
would provide it with an opportunity to access periods of higher demand, improving
the commercial viability of such projects. It would also facilitate greater utilisation of
PSPs as flexible storage resources during periods of constrained supply, thereby
supporting system flexibility. In view of the growing operational and under-
construction capacity of PSPs and the need for flexible reserves like PSPs, the
Commission is of the view that PSPs may be permitted to participate in the existing
HP-DAM segment.
7. In view of the above, the Commission proposes the inclusion of PSPs as an
eligible category of generating stations for participation in the existing HP-DAM
segment on Power Exchanges. Accordingly, the Commission proposes to initiate suo
motu proceedings on the aforesaid proposal and hear the parties in accordance with
Regulation 56 of the Conduct of Business Regulations, 2023, for which a public
notice is being issued. Meanwhile, the parties are directed to file their written
submissions within 15 days from the date of this order.
Sd./- Sd./- Sd./- Sd./-
